265	def recommend_merkle_deployment(
266	    capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size"
267	) -> MerkleStorageProfile:
268	    """Return the :class:`MerkleStorageProfile` fitting deployment budgets.
269	
270	    Unlike :func:`recommend`, which only minimises the tree height, this
271	    enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height``
272	    from 1 to 8 — keeps those whose ``leaf_count`` covers ``capacity`` and
273	    that satisfy every set budget, and ranks the feasible set.
274	
275	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
276	    must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
277	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on one signature wire
278	    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), on one
279	    standalone proof wire length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`)
280	    and on the verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s
281	    ``steps``). Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive,
282	    non-boolean integer, and at least one entry must be set.
283	
284	    ``prefer="size"`` ranks candidates lexicographically by signature wire
285	    length, proof wire length, checkpoint bytes, steps, leaf count, ``w`` and
286	    ``height``; ``prefer="speed"`` minimises steps first and then applies the
287	    same remaining order. The first candidate after sorting is returned as a
288	    :class:`MerkleStorageProfile`.
289	
290	    A non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a tuple of the wrong length,
291	    an illegal member, an out-of-range ``capacity``, an unknown ``prefer``
292	    value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError``. The
293	    function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes
294	    no state.
295	    """
296	    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
297	        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 4-tuple of budget limits")
298	    if len(budgets) != 4:
299	        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly four entries")
300	    if (
301	        isinstance(capacity, bool)
302	        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
303	        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
304	    ):
305	        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
306	    if prefer not in ("size", "speed"):
307	        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')
308	
309	    labels = ("checkpoint", "signature", "proof", "steps")
310	    limits = []
311	    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
312	        if budget is None:
313	            limits.append(None)
314	        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
315	            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
316	        else:
317	            limits.append(budget)
318	    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
319	        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
320	    checkpoint_limit, signature_limit, proof_limit, steps_limit = limits
321	
322	    feasible = []
323	    for w in (4, 8):
324	        for height in range(1, 9):
325	            storage = merkle_storage_profile(w, height)
326	            if storage.leaf_count < capacity:
327	                continue
328	            if checkpoint_limit is not None and storage.checkpoint_bytes > checkpoint_limit:
329	                continue
330	            if signature_limit is not None and storage.signature_wire_bytes > signature_limit:
331	                continue
332	            if proof_limit is not None and storage.proof_wire_bytes > proof_limit:
333	                continue
334	            steps = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height).steps
335	            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:
336	                continue
337	            feasible.append((storage, steps))
338	    if not feasible:
339	        raise ValueError("no Merkle configuration fits the requested capacity and budgets")
340	
341	    def ranking(candidate: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
342	        storage, steps = candidate
343	        ordered = (
344	            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
345	            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
346	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
347	            steps,
348	            storage.leaf_count,
349	            storage.w,
350	            storage.height,
351	        )
352	        if prefer == "speed":
353	            return (steps,) + ordered
354	        return ordered
355	
356	    feasible.sort(key=ranking)
357	    return feasible[0][0]

400	def merkle_deployment_frontier(
401	    capacity: Any, budgets: Any
402	) -> tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, ...]:
403	    """Return every feasible, non-dominated ordinary Merkle deployment as a tuple.
404	
405	    Where :func:`recommend_merkle_deployment` ranks the feasible configs and
406	    returns one, this function keeps the whole Pareto frontier so a caller can
407	    inspect the trade-off between storage, signature, proof and verification
408	    costs: it enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times
409	    ``height`` from 1 to 8 — whose ``leaf_count`` covers ``capacity``, keeps
410	    those satisfying every set budget, reusing
411	    :func:`merkle_storage_profile` for the wire sizes and
412	    :func:`profile` for the per-signature verifier hash-chain step count, and
413	    drops every dominated candidate.
414	
415	    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
416	    must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
417	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on one signature wire
418	    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), on one
419	    standalone proof wire length
420	    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`) and on the per-signature
421	    verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s ``steps``).
422	    Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean
423	    integer, and at least one entry must be set; every bound is inclusive.
424	
425	    A feasible profile *A* dominates another feasible profile *B* when
426	    ``A`` is no greater than ``B`` on all four metrics — checkpoint bytes,
427	    signature wire bytes, proof wire bytes and verifier steps — and strictly
428	    smaller on at least one; every dominated candidate is dropped and the
429	    survivors are deduplicated by value. No preference is applied, so a
430	    configuration trading speed for size (or the reverse) is never discarded
431	    ahead of the dominance test. The returned tuple is sorted stably and
432	    ascending by verifier steps, signature wire bytes, proof wire bytes,
433	    checkpoint bytes, leaf count, ``w`` and ``height``.
434	
435	    A non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a wrong-length or otherwise
436	    illegal ``budgets`` tuple, an out-of-range ``capacity`` or the absence of
437	    any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it
438	    draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes no state.
439	    """
440	    limits = _validate_deployment_budgets(budgets)
441	    if (
442	        isinstance(capacity, bool)
443	        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
444	        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
445	    ):
446	        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
447	    checkpoint_limit, signature_limit, proof_limit, steps_limit = limits
448	
449	    candidates: list[tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int]] = []
450	    for w in (4, 8):
451	        for height in range(1, 9):
452	            storage = merkle_storage_profile(w, height)
453	            if storage.leaf_count < capacity:
454	                continue
455	            if checkpoint_limit is not None and storage.checkpoint_bytes > checkpoint_limit:
456	                continue
457	            if signature_limit is not None and storage.signature_wire_bytes > signature_limit:
458	                continue
459	            if proof_limit is not None and storage.proof_wire_bytes > proof_limit:
460	                continue
461	            steps = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height).steps
462	            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:
463	                continue
464	            candidates.append((storage, steps))
465	    if not candidates:
466	        raise ValueError("no Merkle configuration fits the requested capacity and budgets")
467	
468	    def dominates(
469	        a: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int],
470	        b: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int],
471	    ) -> bool:
472	        a_storage, a_steps = a
473	        b_storage, b_steps = b
474	        no_worse = (
475	            a_storage.checkpoint_bytes <= b_storage.checkpoint_bytes
476	            and a_storage.signature_wire_bytes <= b_storage.signature_wire_bytes
477	            and a_storage.proof_wire_bytes <= b_storage.proof_wire_bytes
478	            and a_steps <= b_steps
479	        )
480	        strictly_better = (
481	            a_storage.checkpoint_bytes < b_storage.checkpoint_bytes
482	            or a_storage.signature_wire_bytes < b_storage.signature_wire_bytes
483	            or a_storage.proof_wire_bytes < b_storage.proof_wire_bytes
484	            or a_steps < b_steps
485	        )
486	        return no_worse and strictly_better
487	
488	    non_dominated = [
489	        candidate
490	        for candidate in candidates
491	        if not any(dominates(other, candidate) for other in candidates)
492	    ]
493	
494	    unique: list[MerkleStorageProfile] = []
495	    seen: set[MerkleStorageProfile] = set()
496	    for storage, _steps in non_dominated:
497	        if storage not in seen:
498	            seen.add(storage)
499	            unique.append(storage)
500	
501	    unique.sort(
502	        key=lambda storage: (
503	            profile("merkle", w=storage.w, height=storage.height).steps,
504	            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
505	            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
506	            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
507	            storage.leaf_count,
508	            storage.w,
509	            storage.height,
510	        )
511	    )
512	    return tuple(unique)

516	class MerkleStorageProfile:
517	    """Frozen on-the-wire byte sizes for one Merkle ``(w, height)`` choice.
518	
519	    Every value is a size in bytes of the matching serialised object,
520	    excluding Python object overhead:
521	
522	    - ``w`` / ``height`` echo the validated parameters;
523	    - ``leaf_count`` is ``L = 2 ** height`` W-OTS leaves;
524	    - ``signature_wire_bytes`` (``S``) is one ``MerkleSignature.to_bytes``

def recommend(capacity: Any, prefer: str = "size") -> Params:
    """Return the Merkle :class:`Params` covering ``capacity`` signatures.

    ``capacity`` must be an integer from 1 to 256 (non-bool); the height is
    the smallest one with ``2 ** height >= capacity`` and at least 1.
    ``prefer="size"`` picks ``w=8`` (shorter signatures), ``prefer="speed"``
    picks ``w=4`` (fewer chain steps). Anything else raises ``ValueError``.
    """
    if (
        isinstance(capacity, bool)
        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
    if prefer == "size":
        w = 8
    elif prefer == "speed":
        w = 4
    else:
        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')
    height = max(1, (capacity - 1).bit_length())
    return profile("merkle", w=w, height=height)


def recommend_merkle_deployment(
    capacity: Any, budgets: Any, prefer: Any = "size"
) -> MerkleStorageProfile:
    """Return the :class:`MerkleStorageProfile` fitting deployment budgets.

    Unlike :func:`recommend`, which only minimises the tree height, this
    enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times ``height``
    from 1 to 8 — keeps those whose ``leaf_count`` covers ``capacity`` and
    that satisfy every set budget, and ranks the feasible set.

    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
    must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on one signature wire
    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), on one
    standalone proof wire length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`)
    and on the verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s
    ``steps``). Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive,
    non-boolean integer, and at least one entry must be set.

    ``prefer="size"`` ranks candidates lexicographically by signature wire
    length, proof wire length, checkpoint bytes, steps, leaf count, ``w`` and
    ``height``; ``prefer="speed"`` minimises steps first and then applies the
    same remaining order. The first candidate after sorting is returned as a
    :class:`MerkleStorageProfile`.

    A non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a tuple of the wrong length,
    an illegal member, an out-of-range ``capacity``, an unknown ``prefer``
    value or the absence of any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError``. The
    function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes
    no state.
    """
    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 4-tuple of budget limits")
    if len(budgets) != 4:
        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly four entries")
    if (
        isinstance(capacity, bool)
        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
    if prefer not in ("size", "speed"):
        raise ValueError('prefer must be "size" or "speed"')

    labels = ("checkpoint", "signature", "proof", "steps")
    limits = []
    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
        if budget is None:
            limits.append(None)
        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
        else:
            limits.append(budget)
    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
    checkpoint_limit, signature_limit, proof_limit, steps_limit = limits

    feasible = []
    for w in (4, 8):
        for height in range(1, 9):
            storage = merkle_storage_profile(w, height)
            if storage.leaf_count < capacity:
                continue
            if checkpoint_limit is not None and storage.checkpoint_bytes > checkpoint_limit:
                continue
            if signature_limit is not None and storage.signature_wire_bytes > signature_limit:
                continue
            if proof_limit is not None and storage.proof_wire_bytes > proof_limit:
                continue
            steps = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height).steps
            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:
                continue
            feasible.append((storage, steps))
    if not feasible:
        raise ValueError("no Merkle configuration fits the requested capacity and budgets")

    def ranking(candidate: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        storage, steps = candidate
        ordered = (
            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
            steps,
            storage.leaf_count,
            storage.w,
            storage.height,
        )
        if prefer == "speed":
            return (steps,) + ordered
        return ordered

    feasible.sort(key=ranking)
    return feasible[0][0]


def _validate_deployment_budgets(budgets: Any) -> tuple[int | None, ...]:
    """Validate the four-tuple of deployment budget limits."""
    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):
        raise TypeError("budgets must be a 4-tuple of budget limits")
    if len(budgets) != 4:
        raise ValueError("budgets must contain exactly four entries")
    labels = ("checkpoint", "signature", "proof", "steps")
    limits = []
    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
        if budget is None:
            limits.append(None)
        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
        else:
            limits.append(budget)
    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):
        raise ValueError("at least one budget must be set")
    return tuple(limits)


def _validate_transport_budgets(budgets: Any) -> tuple[int | None, ...]:
    """Validate the four-tuple of checkpoint/batch/multi-proof/steps limits."""
    if not isinstance(budgets, tuple):

    labels = ("checkpoint", "batch", "multiproof", "steps")
    limits = []
    for label, budget in zip(labels, budgets):
        if budget is None:
            limits.append(None)
        elif isinstance(budget, bool) or not isinstance(budget, int) or budget < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{label} budget must be None or a positive integer")
        else:
            limits.append(budget)
    if all(limit is None for limit in limits):

def merkle_deployment_frontier(
    capacity: Any, budgets: Any
) -> tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, ...]:
    """Return every feasible, non-dominated ordinary Merkle deployment as a tuple.

    Where :func:`recommend_merkle_deployment` ranks the feasible configs and
    returns one, this function keeps the whole Pareto frontier so a caller can
    inspect the trade-off between storage, signature, proof and verification
    costs: it enumerates every Merkle candidate — ``w`` in ``(4, 8)`` times
    ``height`` from 1 to 8 — whose ``leaf_count`` covers ``capacity``, keeps
    those satisfying every set budget, reusing
    :func:`merkle_storage_profile` for the wire sizes and
    :func:`profile` for the per-signature verifier hash-chain step count, and
    drops every dominated candidate.

    ``capacity`` must be a non-boolean integer from 1 to 256. ``budgets``
    must be a four-tuple, in order: an upper bound on the checkpoint bytes
    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`), on one signature wire
    length (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.signature_wire_bytes`), on one
    standalone proof wire length
    (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.proof_wire_bytes`) and on the per-signature
    verifier hash-chain step count (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s ``steps``).
    Each entry is either ``None`` (no bound) or a positive, non-boolean
    integer, and at least one entry must be set; every bound is inclusive.

    A feasible profile *A* dominates another feasible profile *B* when
    ``A`` is no greater than ``B`` on all four metrics — checkpoint bytes,
    signature wire bytes, proof wire bytes and verifier steps — and strictly
    smaller on at least one; every dominated candidate is dropped and the
    survivors are deduplicated by value. No preference is applied, so a
    configuration trading speed for size (or the reverse) is never discarded
    ahead of the dominance test. The returned tuple is sorted stably and
    ascending by verifier steps, signature wire bytes, proof wire bytes,
    checkpoint bytes, leaf count, ``w`` and ``height``.

    A non-tuple ``budgets`` raises ``TypeError``; a wrong-length or otherwise
    illegal ``budgets`` tuple, an out-of-range ``capacity`` or the absence of
    any feasible candidate raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it
    draws no randomness, generates no keys and changes no state.
    """
    limits = _validate_deployment_budgets(budgets)
    if (
        isinstance(capacity, bool)
        or not isinstance(capacity, int)
        or not 1 <= capacity <= _MAX_CAPACITY
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"capacity must be an integer between 1 and {_MAX_CAPACITY}")
    checkpoint_limit, signature_limit, proof_limit, steps_limit = limits

    candidates: list[tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int]] = []
    for w in (4, 8):
        for height in range(1, 9):
            storage = merkle_storage_profile(w, height)
            if storage.leaf_count < capacity:
                continue
            if checkpoint_limit is not None and storage.checkpoint_bytes > checkpoint_limit:
                continue
            if signature_limit is not None and storage.signature_wire_bytes > signature_limit:
                continue
            if proof_limit is not None and storage.proof_wire_bytes > proof_limit:
                continue
            steps = profile("merkle", w=w, height=height).steps
            if steps_limit is not None and steps > steps_limit:
                continue
            candidates.append((storage, steps))
    if not candidates:
        raise ValueError("no Merkle configuration fits the requested capacity and budgets")

    def dominates(
        a: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int],
        b: tuple[MerkleStorageProfile, int],
    ) -> bool:
        a_storage, a_steps = a
        b_storage, b_steps = b
        no_worse = (
            a_storage.checkpoint_bytes <= b_storage.checkpoint_bytes
            and a_storage.signature_wire_bytes <= b_storage.signature_wire_bytes
            and a_storage.proof_wire_bytes <= b_storage.proof_wire_bytes
            and a_steps <= b_steps
        )
        strictly_better = (
            a_storage.checkpoint_bytes < b_storage.checkpoint_bytes
            or a_storage.signature_wire_bytes < b_storage.signature_wire_bytes
            or a_storage.proof_wire_bytes < b_storage.proof_wire_bytes
            or a_steps < b_steps
        )
        return no_worse and strictly_better

    non_dominated = [
        candidate
        for candidate in candidates
        if not any(dominates(other, candidate) for other in candidates)
    ]

    unique: list[MerkleStorageProfile] = []
    seen: set[MerkleStorageProfile] = set()
    for storage, _steps in non_dominated:
        if storage not in seen:
            seen.add(storage)
            unique.append(storage)

    unique.sort(
        key=lambda storage: (
            profile("merkle", w=storage.w, height=storage.height).steps,
            storage.signature_wire_bytes,
            storage.proof_wire_bytes,
            storage.checkpoint_bytes,
            storage.leaf_count,
            storage.w,
            storage.height,
        )
    )
    return tuple(unique)

def _validate_transport_weights(weights: Any) -> tuple[int, ...]:
    """Validate the five-tuple of non-negative cost weights."""
    if not isinstance(weights, tuple):
        raise TypeError("weights must be a 5-tuple of non-negative integer weights")
    if len(weights) != 5:
        raise ValueError("weights must contain exactly five entries")
    for weight in weights:
        if isinstance(weight, bool) or not isinstance(weight, int) or weight < 0:
            raise ValueError("every weight must be a non-boolean non-negative integer")
    if not any(weight > 0 for weight in weights):
        raise ValueError("at least one weight must be positive")
    return weights


def recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted(
    capacity: Any,
    indices: Any,
    budgets: Any,
    weights: Any,
) -> MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile:
    """Pick one joint deployment by weighted normalised costs.

    Computes :func:`merkle_transport_deployment_frontier` exactly once and
    ranks the returned joint deployments by a caller-supplied linear score
    over five costs: the batch-proof wire bytes
    (:attr:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile.batch`), the multi-proof wire
    bytes (:attr:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile.multi`), the carried
    multi-proof node count (:attr:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile.nodes`),
    the checkpoint bytes (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`) and
    the per-signature verifier hash-chain steps (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s
    ``steps``).

    ``weights`` must be a five-tuple in that same order — batch-proof bytes,
    multi-proof bytes, carried nodes, checkpoint bytes and per-signature
    chain steps. Every weight must be a non-boolean, non-negative integer
    and at least one must be positive. Each of the five costs is min-max
    normalised over the whole frontier as ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with
    a zero span scoring ``0``; the weighted score is the sum of the five
    normalised costs times their weights, compared as exact rationals
    (``fractions.Fraction``) with no floating point anywhere. The survivor
    with the smallest score is returned; equal scores are broken ascending
    by checkpoint bytes, leaf count, ``w`` and ``height``, exactly like the
    tail of every other joint-deployment ranking. The candidate enumeration
    and Pareto filtering are not duplicated: the frontier is the only source
    of candidates and is called exactly once.

    ``capacity``, ``indices`` and the four-tuple ``budgets`` follow
    :func:`merkle_transport_deployment_frontier`'s types, ranges,
    inclusive-budget, exception and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so
    a violation raises exactly as that function does (and is screened before
    ``weights``). A non-tuple ``weights`` raises ``TypeError``; a
    wrong-length tuple or a boolean, negative, non-integer or all-zero
    weight raises ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no
    randomness, generates no keys and changes no state.
    """
    frontier = merkle_transport_deployment_frontier(capacity, indices, budgets)
    _validate_transport_weights(weights)

    def metrics(
        deployment: MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile,
    ) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
        return (
            deployment.batch,
            deployment.multi,
            deployment.nodes,
            deployment.config.checkpoint_bytes,
            profile(
                "merkle",
                w=deployment.config.w,
                height=deployment.config.height,
            ).steps,
        )

    metric_rows = tuple(metrics(deployment) for deployment in frontier)
    spans = tuple(
        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
        for i in range(5)
    )

    def ranking(
        deployment: MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile,
    ) -> tuple[Fraction, int, int, int, int]:
        score = Fraction(0)
        for value, weight, (low, high) in zip(metrics(deployment), weights, spans):
            if high > low:
                score += weight * Fraction(value - low, high - low)
        config = deployment.config
        return (
            score,
            config.checkpoint_bytes,
            config.leaf_count,
            config.w,
            config.height,
        )

    return min(frontier, key=ranking)


def recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted_scenarios(
    capacity: Any,
    indices: Any,
    budgets: Any,
    scenarios: Any,
) -> MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile:
    """Pick one joint deployment minimising worst regret over scenarios.

    The preference-drift-robust counterpart of
    :func:`recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted`: instead of
    trusting one five-tuple of cost weights, it evaluates several weight
    scenarios at once and picks the member of
    :func:`merkle_transport_deployment_frontier`'s returned joint-deployment
    frontier with the smallest worst-case regret — the maximum, over
    scenarios, of how much worse the chosen deployment scores than the best
    deployment for that scenario. The five weighted costs are the same ones
    :func:`recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted` ranks: the
    batch-proof wire bytes (:attr:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile.batch`),
    the multi-proof wire bytes
    (:attr:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile.multi`), the carried multi-proof
    node count (:attr:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile.nodes`), the
    checkpoint bytes (:attr:`MerkleStorageProfile.checkpoint_bytes`) and the
    per-signature verifier hash-chain steps (``profile("merkle", ...)``'s
    ``steps``).

    ``scenarios`` must be a non-empty tuple; each member must itself be a
    five-tuple in the order batch-proof bytes, multi-proof bytes, carried
    nodes, checkpoint bytes and per-signature chain steps. Every weight must
    be a non-boolean, non-negative integer and at least one weight of each
    scenario must be positive; repeated scenarios are counted separately.

    The joint-deployment frontier is computed exactly once and is the only
    source of candidates — the candidate enumeration and Pareto filtering
    are not duplicated. Each of the five costs is min-max normalised over
    the whole frontier as ``(x - min) / (max - min)``, with a zero span
    scoring ``0``. For each scenario, a candidate's score is the weighted
    sum of its five normalised costs divided by the scenario's weight
    total, all compared as exact rationals (``fractions.Fraction``) with no
    floating point anywhere. Each scenario's own minimum score is then
    subtracted from every candidate's score to give that scenario's regret;
    deployments are ranked first by the greatest regret over the scenarios
    (the minimax-regret choice), then by the sum of the regrets, then by
    the tuple of per-scenario scores, all ascending. Every ranking finishes
    with the same ascending tie-break as every other joint-deployment
    ranking — checkpoint bytes, leaf count, ``w`` and ``height`` — and the
    first survivor is returned as a
    :class:`MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile`.

    ``capacity``, ``indices`` and the four-tuple ``budgets`` follow
    :func:`merkle_transport_deployment_frontier`'s types, ranges,
    inclusive-budget, exception and no-feasible-candidate rules exactly, so
    a violation raises exactly as that function does (and is screened
    before ``scenarios``). A non-tuple ``scenarios`` or scenario member, or
    a non-integer weight, raises ``TypeError``; an empty scenario tuple, a
    wrong-length scenario, or a boolean, negative or all-zero weight raises
    ``ValueError``. The function is pure: it draws no randomness, generates
    no keys and changes no state.
    """
    frontier = merkle_transport_deployment_frontier(capacity, indices, budgets)
    validated_scenarios = _validate_weight_scenarios(scenarios)

    def metrics(
        deployment: MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile,
    ) -> tuple[int, int, int, int, int]:
        return (
            deployment.batch,
            deployment.multi,
            deployment.nodes,
            deployment.config.checkpoint_bytes,
            profile(
                "merkle",
                w=deployment.config.w,
                height=deployment.config.height,
            ).steps,
        )

    metric_rows = tuple(metrics(deployment) for deployment in frontier)
    spans = tuple(
        (min(row[i] for row in metric_rows), max(row[i] for row in metric_rows))
        for i in range(5)
    )

    def normalised(row: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[Fraction, ...]:
        return tuple(
            Fraction(value - low, high - low) if high > low else Fraction(0)
            for value, (low, high) in zip(row, spans)
        )

    normalised_rows = tuple(normalised(row) for row in metric_rows)
    scenario_totals = tuple(sum(weights) for weights in validated_scenarios)

    def scenario_scores(row: tuple[Fraction, ...]) -> tuple[Fraction, ...]:
        return tuple(
            sum(
                (weight * component for weight, component in zip(weights, row)),
                Fraction(0),
            )
            / weight_total
            for weights, weight_total in zip(validated_scenarios, scenario_totals)
        )

    score_rows = tuple(scenario_scores(row) for row in normalised_rows)
    scenario_best = tuple(
        min(row[scenario_index] for row in score_rows)
        for scenario_index in range(len(validated_scenarios))
    )

    def ranking(
        entry: tuple[MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile, tuple[Fraction, ...]],
    ) -> tuple[Fraction, Fraction, tuple[Fraction, ...], int, int, int, int]:
        deployment, scores = entry
        regrets = tuple(
            score - best for score, best in zip(scores, scenario_best)
        )
        config = deployment.config
        return (
            max(regrets),
            sum(regrets, Fraction(0)),
            scores,
            config.checkpoint_bytes,
            config.leaf_count,
            config.w,
            config.height,
        )

    return min(zip(frontier, score_rows), key=ranking)[0]

122	multiproof_encode proof bytes over the batch, the envelope and generation
123	g+1, again under the same single (g, g+1) claim.

309	_PUBLIC_KEY_MAGIC = b"PQALPUB\0"
310	_SIGNATURE_MAGIC = b"PQALSIG\0"
311	_CODEC_VERSION = 1
312	_CODEC_HEADER_BYTES = 8 + 1 + 2 + 2
313	
314	_CHECKPOINT_MAGIC = b"PQALCP\0\0"

320	def _validate_bits(bits: Any) -> int:
321	    if isinstance(bits, bool) or not isinstance(bits, int) or not 1 <= bits <= BITS:
322	        raise ValueError(f"bits must be a non-boolean integer between 1 and {BITS}")
323	    return bits
324	
325	
326	def _validate_container(elements: Any, label: str) -> None:
327	    if not isinstance(elements, tuple):
328	        raise TypeError(f"{label} collection must be a tuple of {HASH_BYTES}-byte values")
329	    for element in elements:
330	        if not isinstance(element, bytes):
331	            raise TypeError(f"every {label} must be bytes")
332	        if len(element) != HASH_BYTES:
333	            raise ValueError(f"every {label} must be exactly {HASH_BYTES} bytes")
334	
335	
336	def _encode_v1(magic: bytes, bits: int, elements: tuple[bytes, ...]) -> bytes:
337	    """Shared v1 layout: magic, version, ``bits``, element count, elements."""
338	    return (
339	        magic
340	        + bytes((_CODEC_VERSION,))
341	        + bits.to_bytes(2, "big")
342	        + len(elements).to_bytes(2, "big")
343	        + b"".join(elements)
344	    )
345

347	def _decode_v1(data: Any, magic: bytes, name: str, *, is_key: bool) -> tuple[int, tuple[bytes, ...]]:
348	    """Parse a v1 blob into ``(bits, elements)``; ``name`` labels errors.
349	
350	    Keys carry ``2 * bits`` elements, signatures carry ``bits``.
351	    """
352	    if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
353	        raise TypeError(f"{name} data must be bytes or bytearray")
354	    data = bytes(data)
355	    if len(data) < _CODEC_HEADER_BYTES:
356	        raise ValueError(f"{name} encoding is truncated")
357	    if data[:8] != magic:
358	        raise ValueError(f"bad {name} magic")
359	    if data[8] != _CODEC_VERSION:
360	        raise ValueError(f"unsupported {name} version: {data[8]}")
361	    bits = int.from_bytes(data[9:11], "big")
362	    _validate_bits(bits)
363	    element_count = int.from_bytes(data[11:13], "big")
364	    expected_count = 2 * bits if is_key else bits
365	    if element_count != expected_count:
366	        raise ValueError("element count does not match bits")
367	    expected_length = _CODEC_HEADER_BYTES + element_count * HASH_BYTES
368	    if len(data) < expected_length:
369	        raise ValueError(f"{name} encoding is truncated")
370	    if len(data) > expected_length:
371	        raise ValueError(f"trailing data after the {name} encoding")
372	    elements = tuple(
373	        data[_CODEC_HEADER_BYTES + i * HASH_BYTES : _CODEC_HEADER_BYTES + (i + 1) * HASH_BYTES]
374	        for i in range(element_count)
375	    )
376	    return bits, elements

379	def _as_bytes(message: Any) -> bytes:
380	    if isinstance(message, bytes):
381	        return message
382	    if isinstance(message, bytearray):
383	        return bytes(message)
384	    if isinstance(message, str):
385	        return message.encode("utf-8")
386	    raise TypeError("message must be bytes, bytearray or str")

389	def message_digest(message: Any) -> bytes:
390	    """SHA-256 digest of the message."""
391	    return hashlib.sha256(_as_bytes(message)).digest()
392	
393	
394	def message_bits(message: Any, *, bits: int = BITS) -> tuple[int, ...]:
395	    """Expand the digest into ``bits`` bits, most significant bit first."""
396	    if not isinstance(bits, int) or not 1 <= bits <= BITS:
397	        raise ValueError(f"bits must be an integer between 1 and {BITS}")
398	    digest = message_digest(message)
399	    return tuple((digest[index >> 3] >> (7 - (index & 7))) & 1 for index in range(bits))

402	def _secret_digest(secret: bytes) -> bytes:
403	    return hashlib.sha256(_DOMAIN + secret).digest()

406	def _key_to_bytes(key: Any, key_type: type, field_name: str, magic: bytes, label: str) -> bytes:
407	    if not isinstance(key, key_type):
408	        raise TypeError(f"to_bytes must be called on a {key_type.__name__}")
409	    elements = getattr(key, field_name, None)
410	    _validate_container(elements, label)
411	    bits = len(elements) // 2
412	    _validate_bits(bits)
413	    if len(elements) != 2 * bits:
414	        raise ValueError("key must contain exactly 2 * bits elements")
415	    return _encode_v1(magic, bits, elements)

418	@dataclass(frozen=True)
419	class PrivateKey:
420	    """``2 * bits`` secret values: index ``2 * i + b`` belongs to bit ``i``, branch ``b``."""
421	
422	    secrets: tuple[bytes, ...]
423	
424	    @property
425	    def bits(self) -> int:
426	        return len(self.secrets) // 2
427	
428	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytes:
429	        """Serialise to the versioned v1 wire format as ``bytes``.
430	
431	        The layout is the 8-byte magic ``b"PQALPRV\\0"``; the version byte
432	        (1); ``bits`` and the element count (``2 * bits``) as 2 big-endian
433	        bytes each; then every secret in its original position, 32 bytes
434	        each. Encoding is deterministic: the same key always produces the
435	        same bytes. A field corrupted by bypassing the frozen value shape —
436	        a non-tuple container or non-``bytes`` members — raises ``TypeError``;
437	        an out-of-range ``bits``, a wrong element count or a member that is
438	        not exactly 32 bytes raises ``ValueError``. The blob contains the
439	        private secrets in the clear — store it as a secret.
440	        """
441	        return _key_to_bytes(self, PrivateKey, "secrets", _PRIVATE_KEY_MAGIC, "private secret")
442	
443	    @classmethod
444	    def from_bytes(cls, data: Any) -> "PrivateKey":
445	        """Parse ``to_bytes()`` output back into a :class:`PrivateKey`.
446	
447	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
448	        ``TypeError``. A bad magic, an unknown version, an out-of-range
449	        ``bits`` value, an element count that is not ``2 * bits``,
450	        truncation or trailing data raises ``ValueError`` and no instance is
451	        returned. The restored key is equal by value to the original.
452	        """
453	        _bits, secrets = _decode_v1(data, _PRIVATE_KEY_MAGIC, "private key", is_key=True)
454	        return cls(secrets)

495	def keygen(*, bits: int = BITS, token_bytes: Callable[[int], bytes] = secrets.token_bytes) -> tuple[PrivateKey, PublicKey]:
496	    """Generate a fresh one-time key pair."""
497	    if not isinstance(bits, int) or not 1 <= bits <= BITS:
498	        raise ValueError(f"bits must be an integer between 1 and {BITS}")
499	    secrets_tuple = tuple(bytes(token_bytes(HASH_BYTES)) for _ in range(2 * bits))
500	    for secret in secrets_tuple:
501	        if len(secret) != HASH_BYTES:
502	            raise ValueError(f"token_bytes must return {HASH_BYTES} bytes")
503	    private_key = PrivateKey(secrets_tuple)
504	    return private_key, public_key_from(private_key)
505

507	def public_key_from(private_key: PrivateKey) -> PublicKey:
508	    """Recompute the public key from a private key."""
509	    if not isinstance(private_key, PrivateKey):
510	        raise TypeError("private_key must be a PrivateKey")
511	    return PublicKey(tuple(_secret_digest(secret) for secret in private_key.secrets))
512	
513	
514	def sign(message: Any, private_key: PrivateKey) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
515	    """Produce a one-time signature: reveal one secret per digest bit."""
516	    if not isinstance(private_key, PrivateKey):
517	        raise TypeError("private_key must be a PrivateKey")
518	    bits = message_bits(message, bits=private_key.bits)
519	    return tuple(private_key.secrets[2 * index + bit] for index, bit in enumerate(bits))
520	
521	
522	def verify(message: Any, signature: Sequence[bytes], public_key: PublicKey) -> bool:
523	    """Check a signature against the digest bits of ``message``."""
524	    if not isinstance(public_key, PublicKey):
525	        raise TypeError("public_key must be a PublicKey")
526	    materialised = tuple(bytes(part) for part in signature)
527	    if len(materialised) != public_key.bits:
528	        return False
529	    bits = message_bits(message, bits=public_key.bits)
530	    for index, bit in enumerate(bits):
531	        if _secret_digest(materialised[index]) != public_key.digests[2 * index + bit]:
532	            return False
533	    return True

536	class OneTimeSigner:
537	    """Thread-safe, single-use wrapper around a :class:`PrivateKey`.
538	
539	    The first :meth:`sign` call returns the ordinary Lamport signature and
540	    marks the key as used; every later call raises :class:`KeyExhaustedError`.
541	    The guard is per instance and per process — copying the private key,
542	    calling the stateless :func:`sign` directly or reusing the key in another
543	    process is the caller's responsibility. State can be persisted with
544	    :meth:`checkpoint` and restored in another process with
545	    :meth:`from_checkpoint`; the checkpoint contains the private key in the
546	    clear and is protected only by a SHA-256 checksum against accidental
547	    corruption, so callers must store it securely.
548	    """
549	
550	    __slots__ = ("_lock", "_private_key", "_public_key", "_used")
551	
552	    def __init__(self, private_key: PrivateKey) -> None:
553	        if not isinstance(private_key, PrivateKey):
554	            raise TypeError("private_key must be a PrivateKey")
555	        self._restore_state(private_key, public_key_from(private_key), False)
556	
557	    def _restore_state(
558	        self,
559	        private_key: PrivateKey,
560	        public_key: PublicKey,
561	        used: bool,
562	    ) -> None:
563	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
564	        self._private_key = private_key
565	        self._public_key = public_key
566	        self._used = used
567	
568	    @property
569	    def public_key(self) -> PublicKey:
570	        """Public key derived from the wrapped private key (read-only)."""
571	        return self._public_key
572	
573	    @property
574	    def used(self) -> bool:
575	        """``True`` once a signature has been produced (read-only)."""
576	        return self._used
577	
578	    def sign(self, message: Any) -> tuple[bytes, ...]:
579	        """Sign once.
580	
581	        Behaves exactly like :func:`sign` on the first call, accepting
582	        ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``; an unsupported message type raises
583	        ``TypeError`` without consuming the key. Any later call raises
584	        :class:`KeyExhaustedError`. Concurrent calls are serialised so that at
585	        most one of them can succeed.
586	        """
587	        with self._lock:
588	            if self._used:
589	                raise KeyExhaustedError("this one-time signing key has already been used")
590	            signature = sign(message, self._private_key)
591	            self._used = True
592	            return signature
593	
594	    def _checkpoint_bytes(self) -> bytes:
595	        """Serialise the signer state; the caller holds the lock."""
596	        key_blob = self._private_key.to_bytes()
597	        body = (
598	            _CHECKPOINT_MAGIC
599	            + bytes((_CHECKPOINT_VERSION, int(self._used)))
600	            + len(key_blob).to_bytes(4, "big")
601	            + key_blob
602	        )
603	        return body + hashlib.sha256(body).digest()
604	
605	    def checkpoint(self) -> bytes:
606	        """Serialise the signer state (private key plus ``used``) to ``bytes``.
607	
608	        The v1 layout is: the 8-byte magic ``b"PQALCP\\0\\0"``; one byte each
609	        for the version (1) and ``used`` (0 or 1); the length of the nested
610	        private key encoding as 4 big-endian bytes; the complete
611	        :meth:`PrivateKey.to_bytes` output; and finally the SHA-256 of all
612	        preceding content. Encoding is deterministic: the same state always
613	        produces the same bytes.
614	
615	        The checkpoint shares the signing lock, so a concurrent snapshot
616	        reflects the state either immediately before or immediately after an
617	        in-flight :meth:`sign`, never part-way through one. The blob contains
618	        the private key in the clear and the trailing hash only detects
619	        accidental corruption — it provides neither authentication nor
620	        encryption, so store it as a secret.
621	        """
622	        with self._lock:
623	            return self._checkpoint_bytes()
624	
625	    def sign_with_auth_state(
626	        self, message: Any, *, key: Any, generation: Any
627	    ) -> tuple[tuple[bytes, ...], bytes]:
628	        """Sign once and return the advanced state as a v2 auth envelope.
629	
630	        Behaves like :meth:`sign` — same ``bytes``/``bytearray``/``str``
631	        message rules, same one-time Lamport signature and the same post-sign
632	        ``used=True`` state, all under the signing lock — but instead of the
633	        signature alone it returns ``(signature, envelope)``: the first half
634	        is the ordinary immutable signature tuple that :meth:`sign` returns,
635	        and the second is the :func:`auth_state_wrap` v2 envelope (``bytes``)
636	        over the v1 :meth:`checkpoint` bytes of the used state with
637	        ``scheme="lamport"`` and the given ``key`` and ``generation``. The
638	        wrapped checkpoint is byte-for-byte identical to the one
639	        :meth:`checkpoint` returns immediately after signing, so the envelope
640	        is byte-for-byte identical to signing and then wrapping an explicit
641	        checkpoint. Pairing the two halves in one call keeps the signature
642	        and the state it advanced to together, so a caller can never match a
643	        signature against a checkpoint taken at the wrong point under
644	        concurrency.
645	
646	        Every argument is validated before the key is spent: ``key`` is
647	        keyword-only and must be a non-empty ``bytes``/``bytearray`` shared
648	        secret; ``generation`` is keyword-only and must be a non-boolean
649	        integer in ``0 .. 2**64 - 1``. A wrong message or key type raises
650	        ``TypeError``; an empty key or an out-of-range generation raises
651	        ``ValueError``; an already used instance raises
652	        :class:`KeyExhaustedError`. Every failure leaves ``used`` untouched
653	        and returns no partial result. The whole call — signature, ``used``
654	        flip, snapshot and wrapping — linearises with :meth:`sign` and
655	        :meth:`checkpoint` under the same lock, at most one concurrent caller
656	        succeeds, and no randomness is drawn. The envelope is plaintext and
657	        authenticated only; it provides neither encryption nor protection
658	        against replay or rollback on its own.
659	        """
660	        message = _as_bytes(message)
661	        key_bytes = _validate_key(key)
662	        generation_value = _validate_generation(generation, "generation")
663	        with self._lock:
664	            if self._used:
665	                raise KeyExhaustedError("this one-time signing key has already been used")

667	            self._used = True

678	    def from_checkpoint(cls, data: Any) -> "OneTimeSigner":
679	        """Restore a signer from ``checkpoint()`` output without randomness.
680	
681	        ``data`` must be ``bytes`` or ``bytearray``; anything else raises
682	        ``TypeError``. A bad magic, an unknown version, a ``used`` flag that
683	        is not 0 or 1, a private key length field that does not match the
684	        content, an invalid nested private key encoding, truncation, trailing
685	        data or a checksum mismatch raises ``ValueError`` and no instance is
686	        returned. The private key and the public key rebuilt from it are
687	        identical to the original's, so a restored unused signer still allows
688	        exactly one signature and a checkpoint taken after signing restores a
689	        signer whose every call raises :class:`KeyExhaustedError`.
690	        """
691	        if not isinstance(data, (bytes, bytearray)):
692	            raise TypeError("checkpoint data must be bytes or bytearray")
693	        data = bytes(data)
694	        header = _CHECKPOINT_HEADER_BYTES
695	        if len(data) < header + _CHECKPOINT_CHECKSUM_BYTES:
696	            raise ValueError("checkpoint is too short")

699	            raise ValueError("bad checkpoint magic")
700	        if body[8] != _CHECKPOINT_VERSION:
701	            raise ValueError(f"unsupported checkpoint version: {body[8]}")
702	        used_byte = body[9]
703	        if used_byte not in (0, 1):
704	            raise ValueError("used flag must be 0 or 1")
705	        key_length = int.from_bytes(body[10:14], "big")
706	        if len(body) != header + key_length:
707	            raise ValueError("private key length field does not match the checkpoint length")

709	            raise ValueError("checkpoint checksum mismatch")
710	        try:

712	        except (TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
713	            raise ValueError(f"invalid nested private key encoding: {exc}") from exc

"""pqattest - hash-based one-time and few-times signatures, plus a toy KEM.

Public API: keygen / public_key_from / sign / verify / message_bits /
OneTimeSigner / KeyExhaustedError, with a deterministic, versioned v1 binary
codec for the Lamport keys and stateless signatures:
PrivateKey.to_bytes / PrivateKey.from_bytes,
PublicKey.to_bytes / PublicKey.from_bytes,
lamport_signature_to_bytes / lamport_signature_from_bytes, and a versioned
state checkpoint for the signer: OneTimeSigner.checkpoint /
OneTimeSigner.from_checkpoint; the Winternitz
construction: wots_keygen / wots_sign / wots_verify / WOTSPrivateKey /
WOTSPublicKey / WOTSOneTimeSigner / wots_signature_to_bytes /
wots_signature_from_bytes, Merkle-aggregated W-OTS: MerkleSigner /
MerklePublicKey / MerkleSignature / MerkleProof / MerkleBatchProof /
merkle_verify / multiproof_encode / multiproof_verify /
multiproof_verify_bound (the two proof classes' verify_bound and this
function bind a proof to the receiver's expected public key and,
optionally, an explicit leaf-index selection), static
parameter analysis: Params / profile / recommend / recommend_merkle_deployment /
merkle_deployment_frontier /
MerkleStorageProfile / merkle_storage_profile / merkle_transport_profile /
recommend_merkle_transport_deployment / MerkleTransportDeploymentProfile /
merkle_transport_deployment_frontier /
recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted to rank that frontier by a
five-tuple of non-negative weights over min-max-normalised costs with exact
Fraction arithmetic,
recommend_merkle_transport_deployment_weighted_scenarios to rank that same
frontier by the smallest worst-case regret over a non-empty tuple of such
five-weight scenarios, again with exact Fraction arithmetic,
recommend_merkle_transport_workload / MerkleTransportWorkloadProfile /
merkle_transport_workload_frontier /
recommend_merkle_transport_workload_weighted to rank that workload
frontier by a four-tuple of non-negative weights over min-max-normalised
costs (checkpoint bytes, single-group peak, total transport and verifier
steps), the weighted sum divided by the weight total, with exact Fraction
arithmetic,
recommend_merkle_transport_workload_weighted_scenarios to rank that same
workload frontier by the smallest worst-case regret over a non-empty
tuple of such four-weight scenarios, again with exact Fraction
arithmetic,
merkle_mode_frontier /
recommend_merkle_mode_deployment,
recommend_merkle_mode_weighted to rank that mode frontier by a five-tuple
of non-negative weights over min-max-normalised costs (checkpoint bytes,
single-group peak, total transport, verifier steps and carried nodes), the
weighted sum divided by the weight total, with exact Fraction arithmetic,
recommend_merkle_mode_weighted_scenarios to rank that mode frontier by the
smallest worst-case regret over a non-empty tuple of five-weight scenarios
(checkpoint bytes, single-group peak, total transport, verifier steps and
carried nodes) with exact Fraction arithmetic,
MerkleVerifyProfile / merkle_verify_profile,
MerkleVerifyWorkloadProfile / merkle_verify_workload_profile,
MerkleModeCost / merkle_verify_mode_frontier,
merkle_cardinality_frontier for the worst-case-position cardinality
frontier, recommend_merkle_cardinality_deployment to rank that frontier
by one of five preferences, recommend_merkle_cardinality_weighted to
rank it by a five-tuple of non-negative weights over min-max-normalised
costs with exact Fraction arithmetic,
recommend_merkle_verify_mode_weighted to rank the fixed-position joint

tuple of such five-weight scenarios, again with exact Fraction arithmetic,
recommend_merkle_cardinality_weighted_scenarios to rank the
worst-case-position cardinality frontier that same way, by the smallest
worst-case regret over a non-empty tuple of five-weight scenarios with
exact Fraction arithmetic,
recommend_merkle_verify_mode_deployment to rank the fixed-position
